review:
All four prior findings verified against the code on disk, and the new lock-retry code introduces no correctness or security regression.

Prior finding #1: fixed
Prior finding #2: fixed
Prior finding #3: fixed
Prior finding #4: withdrawn

**Verification notes**
- **Smoke script** now passes a temp-dir `configPath` in all four export calls (`scripts/emit-publish-smoke-artifacts.ts:139-170`), so the real registry is untouched.
- **Missing-collection guard** moved to `src/publish/export-service.ts:336`, ahead of content load and the egress audit. The new test asserts the error text and that neither content nor audit is touched.
- **Inaccessible root** now throws the explicit message at `src/publish/identities.ts:104` with the cause attached, covered by a test that also confirms no registry file is created.
- **Doc duplication** withdrawn per the stated decision to keep CLI and Publishing references standalone.

**New code reviewed**
- `acquireIdentityLock` uses zero-wait attempts with a 25 ms sleep bounded by a 5 s deadline. With `flock -w 0` and the SQLite fallback at busy timeout 0, each attempt fails fast instead of blocking the event loop, which fixes the same-process concurrency case the host reproduced. Each attempt closes its SQLite handle or reaps its spawned holder, so no handles leak across retries.
- The regression test forces the SQLite path via an empty `PATH`, checks same-process concurrent allocation, and confirms a held external lock blocks a child process until release. That covers both the fixed bug and the cross-process guarantee.
- FYI only: on heavy contention the flock path can spawn up to roughly 200 short-lived processes over the 5 s window. That is acceptable for an interactive export and needs no change.

items.title: Duplicated Code smell in docs
items.body: Duplicated Code smell in docs. The two identity paragraphs are pasted verbatim into `docs/CLI.md` and `docs/PUBLISHING.md`, so they will drift.
items.suggestion: Keep the full text in PUBLISHING.md and link to it from CLI.md with a one-sentence summary.

items.title: The smoke script calls the export service without `configPath`
items.body: The smoke script calls the export service without `configPath`. After this diff, running it writes throwaway temp-dir keys into the developer's real platform `publish-identities.json` and leaves a `.lock` file there. It is a manual dev script, not CI, so impact is registry clutter rather than data loss.
items.suggestion: Pass `configPath: join(root, "config/config.yml")` in the four export calls, matching the test fixtures.

items.title: Single-document export previously tolerated a document whose collection is absent from config (it just skipped attachment bundling)
items.body: Single-document export previously tolerated a document whose collection is absent from config (it just skipped attachment bundling). It now throws "Collection not configured". The change is consistent with the spec's "root must be accessible" rule, but it runs after the egress audit record is written, and no test covers the new failure.
items.suggestion: Move the guard above the egress audit call and add a one-line regression test for the error.

items.title: `realpath` on a missing collection root throws a raw ENOENT outside the try block, so the user sees a filesystem error rather than the registry-specific guidance the docs promise
items.body: `realpath` on a missing collection root throws a raw ENOENT outside the try block, so the user sees a filesystem error rather than the registry-specific guidance the docs promise.
items.suggestion: Wrap the root resolution in a short error such as "Collection root must exist to resolve publish identities".
